🪖🇮🇱 Israel arms Druze in Suwayda: New military base or prelude to another attack on Syria?
Israeli forces have reportedly deployed weapons, advanced equipment and radar systems to Jabal al-Arab in Syria’s Suwayda province, potentially paving the way for a military base, Syria 360 reports citing local sources.
👉 Local Druze authorities have reportedly barred civilians from approaching or photographing the sites.
The report comes amid warnings from a senior Syrian official, who told The Jerusalem Post on October 19 that Druze armed groups could soon attack Syrian forces to retake Druze villages, potentially with Israeli backing. The official also cited intensified Israeli aerial surveillance over Suwayda and Damascus, alongside alleged Israeli deliveries of weapons and ammunition to the province. 
➡️ Tensions escalated in Suwayda in July 2025, when clashes erupted between Syrian government and Bedouin forces[ on the one side and Druze fighters on the other](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/53923). After Syrian troops entered the province, Israel launched strikes across Syria, including on the General Staff headquarters in Damascus. 
But Israel’s intervention was no act of altruism: the government was exploiting the clashes to expand[ its control over southern Syria](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70780), Asharq Al-Awsat warned at the time.
‼️ Following the fall of Bashar al-Assad, Israel established around 11 military bases and outposts in southern Syria, mostly in Quneitra Governorate, with positions extending north toward Rif Dimashq and Al-Tulul al-Humr sites, and south toward Daraa Governorate, according to the Jusoor portal. Two adjacent bases near Majdal Shams predated Assad’s fall.
The expansion aligns with Israel’s “David Corridor," envisioned as [a route from the occupied Golan Heights](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/54289) through Quneitra, Daraa, and Suwayda to al-Tanf, then east to Deir Ezzor and Iraqi Kurdistan. Although the Syrian government has blocked the proposed eastern leg, Israel continues to entrench itself in southern Syria.

The operation was expected to exceed the intensity of the joint US-Israeli offensive launched in February. Targets included nuclear facilities, power plants and other civilian infrastructure, as well as regime-related sites.
Trump opposed renewing the war before the US midterm elections on November 3. The White House confirmed: "The US will not attack Iran before the elections."
One FT source said it will be "either a deal or an attack," adding that renewed strikes in the coming weeks remain a "realistic scenario" — possibly involving both countries.
